title: Aggregate Limits Held Plan by Plan — Northloop Protect Plans Training Note
content:
**Rule.** Northloop Protect Plans are never pooled: each plan's aggregate limit is its own covered item price, and settlements on one plan never reduce another plan's limit even when both cover items from the same order history.

## The rule restated

- **Whose limit:** every plan has its own aggregate limit.
- **How large:** that limit is the covered item price of that plan's own covered item.
- **What reduces it:** only settlements paid on that same plan. Settlements on any other plan the buyer holds never reduce it, whatever orders the covered items came from.

## Training questions

**A buyer holds two plans. Can the unused limit of one be used toward a claim on the other?**
No. Plans are never pooled; each plan's limit is its own covered item price.

**Two plans cover items bought by the same buyer over the same months. Does a large settlement on one shrink the other's limit?**
No. Settlements on one plan never reduce another plan's limit, even when both cover items from the same order history.

## Hypothetical illustration

A buyer holds Plan A on an item with a covered item price of 400.00 USD and Plan B on an item with a covered item price of 900.00 USD. Settlements of 400.00 USD have been paid on Plan A.

| Plan | Covered item price (aggregate limit) | Settlements paid on this plan | Limit used by settlements on the other plan |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plan A | 400.00 USD | 400.00 USD | None |
| Plan B | 900.00 USD | 0.00 USD | None |

Plan A's settlements have reached its own covered item price; Plan B's aggregate limit is still its own covered item price of 900.00 USD, untouched by anything paid on Plan A.
